request_state.title: RELATIVE ANABELIAN GEOMETRY OF P^1 \ {0, 1, infty} OVER SPEC Z
request_state.claim: Section conjecture and outer Galois representation into Out(pi_1^{et}(P^1 \ {0,1,infty})) isolate rational points with three-point ramification.
request_state.method: Anabelian geometry (Grothendieck, Mochizuki, Stix), étale fundamental groups, section conjecture.

instructions: Does this candidate argue that the positive hyperbolic defect -chi = 1 - 1/x - 1/y - 1/z > 0 (or negative Euler characteristic / hyperbolic area of the triangle curve) forces integer points to be empty?
criteria: level 0: Does not use hyperbolic defect, Euler characteristic, or triangle curvature at all.
level 1: Mentions hyperbolic defect only as background context, relying on modular forms or other tools.
level 2: Uses hyperbolic defect as a necessary condition for finiteness, but does not claim non-existence from it alone.
level 3: Directly claims that -chi > 0 forces non-existence of solutions, or derives contradiction from -chi > 0 alone.

fc_blindness_vulnerability.instructions: Would the mathematical mechanism of this candidate hold equally for the known Fermat-Catalan identities with exponent 2 (7^3 + 13^2 = 2^9 (signature (3, 2, 9), -chi = 1/18 > 0), 1^6 + 2^3 = 3^2 (signature (6, 3, 2), -chi = 1/6 > 0))? Specifically, does the argument fail to use the condition min(x, y, z) >= 3 in a way that breaks down on exponent 2?

criteria.true: The mechanism holds on exponent 2 identities; it is vulnerable to Fermat-Catalan blindness.
criteria.false: The mechanism strictly breaks down or produces a contradiction when one exponent is 2.

criteria.refute_defect_insufficiency: Candidate relies on defect insufficiency; mark BLOCKED with Fermat-Catalan counterexample.

criteria.sound_independent: Candidate does not rely on hyperbolic defect; mechanism is independent.
